question:
Test: `marshmallow_qa/validate_regex_generator_m3_state/files/testcase.py`, test class `RegexGeneratorStateTest`. Run the WHOLE class with pytest from the repository root (pytest id `marshmallow_qa/validate_regex_generator_m3_state/files/testcase.py::RegexGeneratorStateTest`); it contains 12 `test_...` methods and the answer aggregates over ALL of them (the answer is a set, so the order in which the methods run does not matter).

Target function: `URL.RegexMemoizer._regex_generator` defined in `src/marshmallow/validate.py` (nested class `RegexMemoizer` inside class `URL`; module `marshmallow.validate`). The tests call it directly, each time on a fresh `RegexMemoizer` instance and with the module global `_UNICODE_LETTERS` temporarily patched to a test-computed string.

An invocation is one call of the target (one new frame of `_regex_generator`) during the test run. Inside each invocation, the local variable `hostname_variants` is first bound to a list and that same list object may later be mutated in place (an element appended) before the function returns.

Question: across every invocation in every test method, consider every state that the local variable `hostname_variants` holds while the target's frame is executing — i.e. its value right after it is first bound AND its value after every in-place mutation, up to the function's return. (Points where the variable is not yet bound contribute nothing.) Take Python's `repr()` of the whole list in each such state (CPython 3.11; the list's repr contains the `repr()` of each string element, so e.g. a regex backslash inside an element appears doubled, as in `['a\\.b']`, and non-printable characters appear as escape sequences while printable non-ASCII characters appear literally). Report the set of DISTINCT repr strings (exact duplicates, whether from the same or different invocations/methods, are reported once), sorted ascending by plain Python string comparison (`sorted()` on the `str` values, i.e. Unicode code-point order).

Answer format: a JSON object `{"unique_values": [...]}` whose list contains those repr strings (each a JSON string) in the order described. No other keys.
